summary.headline: HDFC Bank Q2 FY27: deposits up 18.8% YoY (incl. ~4pp FCNR(B) lift), NIM down to 3.32%, GNPA 1.11%, ROA 1.8%, quarterly PAT Rs 19.5bn.
summary.overview: Management reported deposit growth of 18.8% YoY and AUM growth of 15.3% YoY, with retail disbursements above Rs 90,000 crore and ECLGS 5.0 contributing Rs 41,000 crore. Asset quality stayed strong with GNPA at 1.11% and credit cost at 44bps. NIM fell to 3.32% and cost of funds was flat QoQ at about 4.4%, driven by time-deposit mix from FCNR(B) inflows. CFO Srinivasan Vaidyanathan guided that Q2 is the margin bottom, with trajectory upward from Q3. The call also covered the CEO transition: Sashidhar Jagdishan is leaving, Anup Bagchi is incoming as MD and CEO, and Kaizad Bharucha has requested early retirement by end-December.

financial_highlights.change: includes ~4 percentage points lift from special FCNR(B) window
down QoQ; management did not give a YoY figure
highest across banks as of Aug 26, 2026

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail disbursements crossed Rs 90,000 crore in Q2 vs Rs 76,000 crore in Q1. Retail assets ex-agri grew about 11.2% YoY in September 2026, up from 9.1% in June and 7.4% in March.

segments.name: Business banking / MSME
segments.commentary: Business banking grew about 28% YoY, helped by ECLGS 5.0. MSME and mid-market EOP loan growth was 23.5% YoY vs 17-18% in prior quarters.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate book grew about 16.4% YoY and 2.8% QoQ. Management said peers grew a couple of percentage points faster and it will not chase corporate growth at the cost of returns.

segments.name: Agri
segments.commentary: Agri GNPA was stable from June to September 2026. Kharif sowing was down only 1.5-2% despite a monsoon shortfall, and management expects crop output variance of 3-5%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects NIM to be neutral to positive going forward, and said Q2 is the bottom with the trajectory upward from Q3.
About 70% of the loan book is floating; the 25bps repo hike in October should be largely factored in by December, which is a tailwind offset by full-quarter FCNR cost impact.
Mix shift towards retail and MSME is expected to lift yields over the next two quarters as back-book runoff (about 20-30% of retail book per year) reprices.
Management will operate LCR within 110-120% and expects LCR glide path to improve with new CEO's strategy, to be unveiled in about a month.
Draft insurance commission norms: comments due in November 2026; management flagged a high impact on bancassurance commissions, to be offset partly by cost and persistency levers.
capex_capacity: Distribution doubled over the last five years and is expected to mature over the next five years; branch deposit productivity described as best-in-class.
Turnaround time on product delivery down 10-15% and service TAT down 30% in the quarter; customer visits per resource per day up about 50% QoQ.
Savings accounts per branch per day up 19% QoQ; core incremental deposits per branch per day up 2.3x vs Q1.
Daily disbursal run rate for key retail and MSME products up 10-20% QoQ.
Headcount has grown about 10% CAGR over five to six years vs volume growth of 18-19%; management expects headcount to stay flat for now and rise in three to four years.
demand_pricing: Deposits grew about Rs 1.57 trillion in the quarter, of which about Rs 1.3 trillion was time deposits; loan growth was about Rs 1.58 trillion, so sources and uses were matched.
Branch-driven deposits are about 80% of total deposits.

Management says the retail CASA ratio is in the late 40s and stable over a long period; structural pressure on CASA is attributed to household savings behaviour and the HDFC Limited borrowing substitution of about Rs 2.6 lakh crore.
Management said MCLR-linked book is a single-digit percentage of the total book, and cost-to-assets is about 1.73-1.74%.
Management said wholesale and retail ROA are broadly comparable when viewed across the 20-F segment disclosures.

qa_highlights.question: When will the retail deposit share start rising, and what is the impact of agri/drought on the book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the retail mix decline to one-off outflows of large deposits (MSME, government, inherited and FCNR(B) leverage deposits), expects momentum to show later. On agri, Kaizad Bharucha said kharif sowing was down only 1.5-2% and agri GNPA was flat June to September; system book growth is single-digit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM decline in line with peers despite a slower corporate build-up?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said cost of funds was flat at about 4.4% due to the FCNR time-deposit mix and borrowing offsets to AT1 call relief. Kaizad Bharucha said back-book repricing in retail (20-30% annual runoff) should show up over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How will FCNR funds be deployed, and what is the margin outlook for next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FCNR funds are treated as deployed since deposit and loan growth were matched; PSL benefit requires deployment. Margins expected neutral to positive, with October repo hike tailwind offset by full-quarter FCNR cost; management said the trajectory is upward from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q2 the margin bottom, and will NIM improve from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO confirmed Q2 is at the bottom, with about 70% floating book repricing by December. Kaizad Bharucha said margin improvement will come from calibrated growth in higher-yield retail and MSME products, not from quarterly shifts in corporate exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Has slippage improvement been driven by mix or by better cohort outcomes?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said slippages are improving across most portfolios, not just from mix, and pointed to absolute slippage figures on the investor deck (Page 19).

qa_highlights.question: Can the industry earn ROE above cost of equity with current CASA dynamics?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the bank still has headroom to gain share in its under-penetrated districts (more than 54% of its 765 districts), where its share is 2-3pp below average. CEO said retail CASA is healthy and the structural CASA pressure is an industry issue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for headcount and operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO expects headcount to stay flat for a while, with a mix shift toward frontline roles, and to rise in three to four years. CFO said productivity is still under-realised, with recent productivity growth in double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Why are LCR and CD ratios weak, and what levers will lift liability growth?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said one-off outflows forced reliance on non-retail deposits with lower LCR cover. CFO said the 110-120% LCR band requires space for growth, and CDs are used opportunistically. Liquidity is described as comfortable beyond the LCR figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of draft insurance norms and the PSL shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the commission cut is high and the bank will look at persistency and cost structure to offset it; comments are due in November. PSL is about 50% at aggregate, with a shortfall in small and marginal farmer sub-targets that the bank is buying in the market.

risks_watch: NIM trajectory: Q2 is said to be the bottom, but the timing and size of repricing benefit versus full-quarter FCNR cost remain unquantified.
LCR at 113% vs 110-120% operating band; new CEO's liability strategy and LCR glide path due in about a month.
CASA ratio pressure from structural household savings shifts and large one-off deposit outflows; retail deposit share has declined in recent quarters.
Leadership transition: new MD and CEO Anup Bagchi takes charge; CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan is leaving; Kaizad Bharucha seeks early retirement by end-December 2026.
Draft insurance commission norms could materially reduce bancassurance income; comments are due in November 2026.
PSL shortfall in small and marginal farmer sub-targets; scarce and costly to source.
Agri credit exposed to uneven monsoon; watch agri GNPA and crop output (management expects a 3-5% variance).
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality, retail momentum and franchise strength, but cautious and deferential on liabilities, LCR and margins, with several questions deferred to incoming CEO Anup Bagchi. Tone turned emotional during the leadership handover.
key_quotes: The fact of the matter is that we are trying to enable a lot of product and service delivery journeys, which can help in having a one-click experience, including on bundling of products depending on the needs of the customer.

Yes, by all account, Parag, that is what we were alluding to, to say that the rate cycle having already kicked in earlier in October, that is a good tailwind on repricing 70% of the loans which are floating.
So, don't go by a quarter phenomenon, Nitin.

Mind you, whilst you're looking at an LCR, there's another metric called liquidity which may not be visible to you all but the institution's liquidity is extremely comfortable and probably slightly more than comfortable.
Yes, we are seeing better across most of these portfolios on the slippages, so it's not mix.

growth.why: No numeric revenue or growth guidance was given; management guided NIM to be neutral to positive with Q2 as the margin bottom, backed by retail disbursements of over Rs 90,000 cr (vs Rs 76,000 cr in Q1), a mix shift to retail/MSME, and repricing of back-book, but no capacity additions were disclosed.

mgmt.note: Sashidhar Jagdishan is leaving and Anup Bagchi is incoming as MD and CEO; Kaizad Bharucha has requested early retirement by end-December; new CEO's strategy not yet detailed.
initiatives: New CEO's strategy to be unveiled in about a month (LCR glide path improvement)
